summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate of Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands-on embedded firmware experience across STM32 microcontrollers, FreeRTOS real-time systems, and Linux-based deployment. Built bare-metal C firmware with interrupt-driven ADC/I2C sampling and closed-loop PWM/UART control on STM32 and Arduino microcontrollers, then debugged hardware-software interface issues through iterative lab bring-up. Comfortable across C/C++, Python, and Git-based Linux engineering workflows.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed wearable gesture-recognition glove firmware integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth microcontrollers to translate hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented an interrupt-driven tap-detection algorithm with z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through structured debugging of the hardware-software interface.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Owned mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and hardware bring-up end-to-end for a 25-member national-competition robotics team.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation in a Linux-based engineering environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 microcontroller firmware in bare-metal embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing, interrupt-driven ADC1 sample capture, and a low-level I2C1 driver for real-time display.
Programmed peripherals directly (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1), achieving 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified functional correctness in Proteus lab simulation.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling for real-time operation and control on an STM32 microcontroller.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to the STM32 over UART for closed-loop hardware-software coordination.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) through structured hardware-software interface debugging; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Implemented two-link IK on an Arduino microcontroller in C++, driving five servos with range-gated contact detection via dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over I2C.
Deployed the Jetson-side firmware bridge as a supervised systemd service with auto-restart, non-root isolation, and static IP networking in a Linux-based engineering environment.
